_**Agent (2026-06-24 14:44:25Z)**_

Now I understand the issue. The TTFT chart has a hardcoded `max: 1200`, so a real spike (you mentioned up to 120s) either gets clipped or, if you raised the cap, the chart would look empty most of the time. The fix is an adaptive y-axis that scales to the actual data while keeping the warn line in view.

Let me add a reusable helper and apply it.

---

_**Agent (2026-06-24 14:44:30Z)**_

<details><summary>Tool use: <b>Edit</b></summary>

```json
{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/Users/gyasisutton/Documents/code/atelier/dashboard/ui/index.html","old_string":"miniLine('ttftChart', [], 800, 1200);\nminiLine('tpsChart', [], 30, 75);","new_string":"miniLine('ttftChart', [], 800, 1200);\nminiLine('tpsChart', [], 30, 75);\n\n// Adaptive y-axis: scale to the live data so a single slow request (e.g. a 120s\n// spike) doesn't flatten everything into the floor — while keeping the warn line\n// in view and a sane minimum range when values are tiny. Reads warn from dataset[1].\nfunction fitY(chart){\n  const warn = Number(chart.data.datasets[1]?.data?.[0]) || 0;\n  const vals = chart.data.datasets[0].data.filter(v => v != null && isFinite(v));\n  const peak = Math.max(warn, ...(vals.length ? vals : [0]));\n  const padded = peak * 1.2;                                   // ~20% headroom\n  const mag = Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(padded || 1)));\n  const nice = Math.ceil(padded / mag) * mag;                  // round up to clean ticks\n  chart.options.scales.y.max = Math.max(nice, warn * 1.25, 1); // keep warn visible\n}"}
```

</details>

_**Agent (2026-06-24 14:44:49Z)**_

Done. Here's what your redpen mark was about and what I changed.

**What you circled:** the **"Time to First Token (ms) · warn 800"** chart in the *Inference Latency – Last 20 Req* panel. Its y-axis was hardcoded to `min:0, max:1200`, so a slow request (you mentioned spikes up to ~120s) would slam into the ceiling and get clipped, while normal low values left the chart looking tall and empty — "long/loud."

**The fix — adaptive y-axis:**
- Added a `fitY(chart)` helper (`dashboard/ui/index.html:641`) that recomputes `scales.y.max` from the live data each refresh: it takes the peak of the current values and the warn line, adds ~20% headroom, and rounds up to a clean tick value — with a floor so the warn threshold always stays visible.
- Wired it into all three chart-update sites: the log-derived TTFT update, the live `ollama_perf` TTFT update, and the tokens/sec chart (same fixed-max problem). Lines ~959, ~977, ~986.

Now the TTFT graph scales to whatever's actually happening — a 120s spike fits in-frame, and quiet periods compress instead of showing a giant empty axis. The 800ms warn dashed line stays in view regardless.

You can reload the dashboard to see it. Want me to also cap the headroom for very small ranges (e.g. always show at least ~1000ms when idle) so the warn line doesn't sit too low, or is the current behavior good?
